webhooks.title: Webhooks — {{name}}

Projects you own are not destroyed — they are kept without an owner and stay manageable by an administrator, since they may be shared with a whole team. Your schema edits keep your name in each project's history.

permission.levelsHint: View: read the project. Edit: change the schema. Deploy: also plan, deploy and roll back on the project's databases. Administrator: also manage access, connections, locks, webhooks and rules.
teams.visibilityNote: A project with no team assigned is visible to everyone. Assigning a team restricts it to that team's members (plus its creator and administrators).
teams.noneAssigned: No team assigned — visible to everyone.
admin.title: Admin console
admin.users.promoteMessage: An instance administrator has access to every project, every connected database, the accounts, the teams and the audit log. They can also appoint other administrators, or take this role away from you.
admin.users.demoteMessage: This person becomes a member again: they keep only what their teams and their own projects give them. It takes effect immediately.

admin.deleteUser.title: Delete {{email}}
admin.deleteUser.consequences: Permanently deletes the account, its sessions, its team memberships and the invitations it sent. Changes it made keep its name in each project's history — that record is not rewritten. If you might still need it, disable the account rather than deleting it.
admin.deleteUser.leaveOwnerless: Leave without an owner (only admins will be able to manage them)
admin.resetPassword.title: Reset password — {{email}}

connections.confirmPull: Are you sure you want to import the schema from this database? This will update your canvas.

connections.strategy.keepColumnDesc: Do not drop column in database; preserve existing data.
connections.strategy.forceCastDesc: Convert existing values to target type using SQL CAST.
connections.strategy.clearDataDesc: Set existing column values to NULL before altering type.
connections.strategy.backfillDefaultDesc: Update existing NULL rows with a replacement value.
connections.strategy.deleteRowsDesc: Delete rows with NULL values before making column NOT NULL.

connections.strategy.useTranslatedTypeDe: Replace the written type with its native equivalent on this engine.
connections.strategy.keepAsWrittenDesc: Deploy the type exactly as written in the canvas.
connections.strategy.proceedDesc: Could not be checked: run the change; the database refuses it if the data conflicts.
connections.strategy.declareKeyDesc: BigQuery does not enforce foreign keys (it is declared NOT ENFORCED): the key is added as it is and the orphan rows stay in the database.
deployment.analyzingDiff: Comparing canvas schema against live database…
deployment.analyzingRisks: Checking the live data for risks before showing any result.
deployment.dropAllHint: Selects “Delete data permanently” on every risk below. Nothing is deleted until you confirm the deployment.
deployment.inSyncDesc: The canvas matches the live database. There are no pending changes.
deployment.noRisksDesc: All detected changes can be safely deployed without data loss risk.

connections.environmentHint: Production asks for the connection's name before every deployment.
deployment.historyEmpty: No deployments yet for this connection.

convertTypes.title: Convert column types
convertTypes.noChanges: Every type in the project is already compatible with this engine.

admin.connections.authSharedHint: Everyone uses the account entered below.
admin.connections.authPersonalHint: Each person enters their own username in Settings → Databases. Yours is used for monitoring.
admin.connections.authNoHolder: Nobody has given their account yet: until someone does, nobody can use this database from Nebula.

personalAccount.tooltip: Your account on this database — change it
personalAccount.missingTooltip: This database asks for your own account: give it to use the database
personalAccount.passwordIntro: Nebula changes your account's password on the database itself, then keeps it encrypted. The old one is not asked for — handy when an administrator created this account for you. If you use this account elsewhere, remember to update it there.
personalAccount.passwordChanged: The password of your account on “{{connection}}” was changed.
settings.sqlAccounts.title: My SQL accounts
settings.sqlAccounts.description: Databases that ask for each person's own account. What you do there from Nebula is done under that account.
admin.connections.readOnlyHint: Nebula refuses to write through this connection: no deployment, no write SQL, no drop, no user management.
admin.connections.forceMonitoring: Impose the watch for changes made outside Nebula
admin.connections.forceMonitoringHint: Every project attached to this connection is watched, at least this often. Project administrators can neither turn it off nor change its settings.
admin.connections.projectTrashedHint: A project in the trash does not hold its database: it can be given to another project. Restored afterwards, it comes back detached from this connection.
admin.connections.projectsHint: On an attached project, the “Deploy” level can deploy to this database, and its administrators can also pull its schema — without seeing or changing its credentials.
admin.connections.projectDatabaseInvalid: Invalid name: letters, digits, _ $ . - only (128 at most).
admin.connections.projectDatabaseDuplica: Another project on this connection already uses this database.

admin.connections.createDatabases: Create the databases that do not exist yet
admin.connections.createDatabasesHint: Empty, with the connection's account. Without this, a missing database makes the first deployment fail.
admin.connections.deleteHint: The stored credentials are erased. The database itself is not touched, and the deployment history is kept.
admin.connections.deleteInUse: This connection is still used by: {{projects}}. These projects will no longer be able to deploy to this database.

dbadmin.sql.saved.empty: No saved query on this connection.

dbadmin.rows.pagingBlocked: Apply or discard the pending changes before changing page.
dbadmin.rows.noIdentity: This row has no complete, readable primary key: it cannot be edited.
dbadmin.rows.notEditable.engine: Read-only: editing rows is not offered on this engine (SQL Server, Oracle, BigQuery).
dbadmin.rows.notEditable.no-primary-key: Read-only: without a primary key (or for a view) nothing identifies a row safely.
dbadmin.rows.notEditable.key-type: Read-only: the primary key's type cannot be compared faithfully.
dbadmin.rows.notEditable.read-access: Your access to this database is read-only.
dbadmin.rows.lock.generated: Computed by the database: never written.
dbadmin.rows.lock.binary: Binary: shown as a hexadecimal excerpt, not editable here.
dbadmin.rows.lock.untyped: SQLite column without a declared type: not editable here, the value would change class.
dbadmin.rows.lock.unsupported: A type that cannot be edited faithfully as text.
dbadmin.rows.lock.partial: Value too long or binary, shown in part: not editable here.
dbadmin.rows.setNullHint: Set the value to NULL (not an empty string)
dbadmin.rows.problem.number: A number is expected (digits, decimal point, exponent).
dbadmin.rows.problem.required: This column does not accept NULL.
dbadmin.rows.requiredHint: No value and no default: the database will probably refuse the row.
dbadmin.rows.editorHint: Values are text in the engine's format. Nothing is sent from here: the change joins the pending ones.
dbadmin.drop.hint: Permanent, data included. Nebula cannot undo it.
dbadmin.users.pick: Select a user or role to see and change its permissions.
dbadmin.users.passwordOnce: Note this password now: Nebula does not keep it and cannot show it again.
dbadmin.users.associateLevel: Access to this database in Nebula

dbadmin.users.associateFailed: The account was created on the database, but could not be associated: {{reason}}
dbadmin.users.mappedToLogin: A database user maps to the server login of the same name, which must already exist.
dbadmin.users.statementHint: Nothing changes until you click Run.

errors.connectionInUse: This connection is still attached to projects.

activity.title: Activity
activity.search: Search an action, a detail, an e-mail…
activity.scopeNote: What is done through Nebula that matters later: deployments, structure and data changes on databases, accounts and permissions, sessions, configuration. Plain reads are not recorded, and schema edits are in each project's own history. Entries cannot be edited or deleted; they are kept for the retention the instance sets (NEBULADB_AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS).
monitoring.title: Watch for changes made outside Nebula
monitoring.hint: Reads the project's databases on a schedule and compares them with the state the last deployment or pull left. A difference nothing in Nebula explains turns on the editor's banner and goes to the project's webhooks. A database that cannot be read is reported as unreachable, never as a change.
monitoring.forced: Imposed by an instance administrator from {{connections}} ({{interval}}). It cannot be turned off here.
monitoring.acknowledgeNote: Note (optional): who is on it, why
notifications.driftAccounts: Accounts or privileges of the database “{{connection}}” were changed outside Nebula.
health.hint: A probe runs each time this opens. What the engine or the account cannot give is said so, never shown as zero.
health.unavailable: Not available for this engine or account.
health.noBlocking: No session is waiting on a lock.
health.blockingHint: The Sessions tab can end the blocking session.
journal.dbside.empty: No session sampled in this period. Take a sample.
journal.dbside.trafficHint: The database server's cumulative counters, difference between two samples. A server restart is ignored. An empty column: the engine has no such counter.
journal.dbside.trafficEmpty: Not two samples yet in this period.
journal.dbside.note: What the database server reports, sampled at intervals: a statement shorter than the interval can be missed. Statements are kept without their values. "Nebula account" is recognised by name only: another application using the same account looks the same. Nebula configures no audit on the server.
journal.author: Author
journal.empty: Nothing recorded for this database over this period.
journal.scopeNote: What was done to this database through Nebula: console opened, connection tested, SQL statements (text cut at 500 characters, duration, rows), deployments and rollbacks, account changes, what the watch found. What was done on the server directly is not here.
journal.queries.measuredHint: Timed by Nebula around the call, opening the connection included — not the database server's own statistics.
journal.queries.empty: No statement has been run through the SQL console over this period.
journal.queries.note: Statements run through Nebula's SQL console, grouped by shape: every value is replaced by ?, and no result is kept. Kept a few days (NEBULADB_QUERY_STATS_RETENTION_DAYS, 30 by default).
journal.indexes.note: Worked out from the statements run through the SQL console (the slowest and the most frequent) and the indexes the database really has. Nothing is run on the database: an index goes through a project's schema, then through a deployment.
journal.indexes.empty: No index to suggest from the statements of this period.
journal.indexes.share: {{executions}} runs, {{total}} in all: {{share}}% of the time measured on this connection.

connections.security.unavailable: Detailed TLS settings and an SSH tunnel need a network database (PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, Oracle) given by a host and a port. With a URI, set TLS in the URI itself.
connections.security.verifyHint: The certificate must be signed by a trusted authority (the system's, or the one below) and carry the host's name. Unchecked, the connection is encrypted but any certificate is accepted.
connections.security.clientHint: The client certificate is only used when the server asks for one. The key is never shown again: leave the field empty to keep the stored one.
connections.security.keyStored: Key stored — leave empty to keep it
connections.security.sshHint: Nebula connects to the SSH server, then to the database from there: the host and port on the Connection tab are the ones the SSH server sees (often localhost or an internal address).
connections.security.sshFingerprintHint: When set, a server presenting another key is refused. Left empty, it is filled in by the first test: compare it with the server's (ssh-keygen -lf) before saving.
connections.security.sshFingerprintSeen: Fingerprint received from the SSH server: {{fingerprint}}. It was copied to the Security tab; check it before saving.
errors.connectionTlsInvalid: Certificates and keys must be PEM text (-----BEGIN …), and a client key goes with its certificate.
errors.connectionSshInvalid: The SSH tunnel needs a server, a user and a password or a readable key (passphrase included), on a connection given by host and port.
errors.connectionSshFailed: The SSH tunnel to the database could not be opened.
admin.sso.hint: Members sign in with their account at your OpenID Connect identity provider (Keycloak, Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace, Authentik, Okta…). Password sign-in stays available.

admin.sso.redirectUriHint: Register it as the client's redirect URI. It follows NEBULADB_PUBLIC_URL when set, otherwise the address you reach Nebula by.
admin.sso.issuerHint: Nebula reads /.well-known/openid-configuration under this address. HTTPS required, except for a provider on this machine (localhost).
admin.sso.secretHint: The secret is never shown again: leave the field empty to keep the stored one. Without a secret the client is public and PKCE alone protects the exchange.
admin.sso.buttonLabel: Name shown on the sign-in button
admin.sso.domainsHint: Comma separated. When filled in, only these addresses can sign in for the first time. An address in these domains is also accepted when the provider does not say it is verified (Entra ID).
admin.sso.autoCreate: Create the account on first sign-in
admin.sso.autoCreateHint: Otherwise only people who already have a Nebula account with the same address can get in. An account created this way is never an administrator.
admin.sso.enabledHint: Adds the button to the sign-in screen.

login.sso.error.no_account: No Nebula account has this address. Ask an administrator for an invitation.
login.sso.error.not_configured: SSO sign-in is not enabled on this instance.
errors.ssoSettingsInvalid: SSO needs an HTTPS issuer URL (HTTP only on localhost), a client ID, and plain domains (example.com).
errors.ssoDiscoveryFailed: The identity provider's configuration could not be read at this address.
errors.ssoNotConfigured: SSO sign-in is not set up on this instance.
folders.name: Folder name
folders.deleteMessage: The projects and subfolders in it move up one level. No project is deleted.
folders.empty: This folder has no project yet.
variants.title: Client variants
variants.hint: A variant is a copy of this project for one client. When you change this project (the original), you choose here which variants receive the changes, and which changes. What the client changed on their side stays theirs unless you choose to replace it.
variants.none: No variant yet. “New client variant” copies this project (schema, layout, locks, initial data).
variants.createHint: A full copy of this project, to adapt for one client. It goes in the same folder.
variants.originalHidden: a project you have no access to
variants.lastSync: Last sent from the original: {{date}} by {{who}}
variants.detachMessage: It becomes a project of its own: it no longer receives the original's changes. Its content does not change.
variants.sync.title: Send the original's changes
variants.sync.hint: Untick what you do not want to send. A conflict is something the client changed too: their version is kept unless you choose the original. What is not sent stays the variant's own and will not be offered again. Positions and layout are never sent.
variants.sync.upToDate: Already up to date: nothing to send.
variants.sync.result: {{applied}} change(s) applied, {{kept}} left to the client
variants.compare.title: Compare two versions
variants.compare.same: No schema difference between these two versions.
errors.variantOfVariant: A variant cannot have variants of its own: create it from the original.
errors.variantNotFound: This project is not a variant of that one.
errors.variantTargetsInvalid: The list of variants sent is not valid.
errors.folderTooDeep: Folders nest at most 5 levels deep.
errors.folderMoveInvalid: A folder cannot go into itself or one of its subfolders.
errors.folderLimitReached: The maximum number of folders has been reached.
errors.folderForbidden: Only whoever made the folder, or an administrator, can change it.
variants.resetMessage: Its structure becomes the original's: the client's adaptations are removed. Its layout is kept. The previous version stays in the History tab.
variants.copyMessage: That variant's structure replaces this one's, adaptations included. Its layout is kept. The previous version stays in the History tab.
variants.trashMessage: It leaves the list of variants and can be restored from the project list's trash.
shareLinks.title: Share links — {{name}}
shareLinks.hint: A share link opens this project's schema read-only, as it is when opened, to anyone who has the address — no account needed. It shows no comments, history, people, connections, environments or data. The owner set in the dictionary is not shown.
shareLinks.disabledOnInstance: Share links are turned off on this instance: an instance administrator can turn them on (Administration → Share links). While they are off, no existing link works.
shareLinks.label: Link label
shareLinks.labelPlaceholder: Who it is for, and why (seen by the team only)
shareLinks.urlOnce: Link address — shown once. Copy it now: it cannot be retrieved later, only revoked.
shareLinks.empty: No share links for this project.
shareLinks.revokeMessage: Anyone using this link will lose access immediately. This cannot be undone.
shareLinks.admin.enabledHint: Project administrators can create read-only links to a project's diagram and dictionary, opened without an account. Turning this off stops every existing link at once, without deleting them.
shareLinks.admin.empty: No share links on this instance.
shareLinks.admin.notKeptHint: This link was made before its address could be kept (or without NEBULADB_SECRET): it can only be revoked.
share.diagramLabel: Schema diagram of {{name}} — drag to move, wheel or + and − to zoom
share.unavailable: This link does not exist or no longer works.
share.rateLimited: Too many requests from this address. Try again in a minute.
share.network: The server is not answering. Try again later.
errors.shareLinkContentInvalid: Choose what the link shows: diagram, dictionary or both.
errors.shareLinkExpiryInvalid: A link is valid for 1 to 365 days.
errors.shareLinksDisabled: Share links are turned off on this instance.
errors.shareLinkNotFound: This link does not exist or no longer works.
errors.shareLinkLimitReached: A project has at most 50 active share links: revoke one first.
backups.destination.s3Hint: AWS S3, MinIO, Scaleway, OVH… Leave the endpoint empty for AWS S3. The keys are encrypted on the instance and never shown again.
backups.destination.s3.pathStyle: Path-style addresses (endpoint/bucket/key), for MinIO and most self-hosted stores
backups.destination.sftpHint: The password or private key is encrypted on the instance and never shown again. The host key fingerprint is required: a server presenting another key is refused.
backups.destination.sftp.fingerprintHint: As ssh-keygen -lf prints it (SHA256:…). Compare it with the server's own.
backups.destination.keepCredentials: Credentials are saved: leave the fields empty to keep them (as long as the server or bucket stays the same).
errors.backupStorageUnreachable: The storage holding this backup cannot be reached: {{reason}}
errors.validationFailed: Some fields are missing or invalid: {{fields}}.
